questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'She ___ to school every day.'
questions.explanation:
Habitual/routine actions use the Simple Present tense.
'She goes to school every day.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'They ___ since last year.'
questions.explanation:
With 'since', use Present Perfect to show an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
'They haven't met since last year.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'He ___ when I arrived.'
questions.explanation:
When one past action happened before another, the earlier action takes the Past Perfect.
'He had left when I arrived.' ✓ (He left first, then I arrived.)
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'I ___ here for five years.'
questions.explanation:
For an action that started in the past and continues to the present, use Present Perfect with 'for'.
'I have lived here for five years.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'She ___ when the phone rang.'
questions.explanation:
Past Continuous is used for an ongoing action that was interrupted by another past action.
'She was studying when the phone rang.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'They ___ the station by 8 p.m. tomorrow.'
questions.explanation:
Future Perfect is used for an action that will be completed before a specific future time.
'They will have reached the station by 8 p.m. tomorrow.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'He ___ three novels so far.'
questions.explanation:
Present Perfect with 'so far' shows actions completed at an unspecified time up to the present.
'He has written three novels so far.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'By the time she arrived, we ___ dinner.'
questions.explanation:
Past Perfect is used for an action completed before another past action.
'By the time she arrived, we had eaten dinner.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'I ___ here since 2010.'
questions.explanation:
Present Perfect Continuous is used for an action that started in the past and is still ongoing, especially with 'since'.
'I have been working here since 2010.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'She ___ her assignment yet.'
questions.explanation:
Present Perfect with 'yet' is used for negative sentences about actions not done up to the present.
'She hasn't completed her assignment yet.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'While I ___ in the park, it started to rain.'
questions.explanation:
'While' introduces a background action in progress — use Past Continuous.
'While I was walking in the park, it started to rain.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'They ___ for two hours when the car broke down.'
questions.explanation:
Past Perfect Continuous shows an ongoing past action that was interrupted by another past action.
'They had been travelling for two hours when the car broke down.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'If he ___ harder, he would pass the exam.'
questions.explanation:
Second Conditional (unreal present/future): If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
'If he studied harder, he would pass the exam.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'She said that she ___ him the previous day.'
questions.explanation:
In reported speech, Simple Past shifts to Past Perfect.
Direct: 'I met him yesterday.' → Reported: 'She said that she had met him the previous day.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'The train ___ before we reached the station.'
questions.explanation:
The train's departure happened before our arrival — both in the past, so the earlier action takes Past Perfect.
'The train had left before we reached the station.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'He ___ in Delhi for ten years before he moved to Mumbai.'
questions.explanation:
Past Perfect shows the earlier of two past events. Living in Delhi preceded moving to Mumbai.
'He had lived in Delhi for ten years before he moved to Mumbai.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'By next year, she ___ her degree.'
questions.explanation:
Future Perfect (will have + past participle) is used for an action that will be completed before a specific future point.
'By next year, she will have completed her degree.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'I ___ such a beautiful painting before.'
questions.explanation:
The sentence refers to a time before a past reference point — use Past Perfect.
'I had never seen such a beautiful painting before.' ✓
(If no past context, Present Perfect 'have never seen' would also work, but Past Perfect fits 'before' in a past narrative.)
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the grammatically correct sentence. (Note: 'know' is a stative verb.)
options: She has been knowing the answer.
questions.explanation:
Stative verbs (know, believe, love, want, etc.) do not take continuous forms.
'She is knowing' / 'She was knowing' are incorrect.
'She knows the answer.' ✓ — Simple Present is correct.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct pair of words:
'No sooner ___ he entered the room ___ the lights went out.'
questions.explanation:
'No sooner...than' requires the Past Perfect inversion in the first clause.
Correct: 'No sooner had he entered the room than the lights went out.' ✓
(Not 'when' — 'no sooner...than' is the fixed collocation.)
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'She wished she ___ harder for the exam.'
questions.explanation:
After 'wish' referring to an unreal past situation, use Past Perfect.
'She wished she had studied harder for the exam.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'It is time we ___ home.'
questions.explanation:
After 'It is time', use the Past Simple (subjunctive) even though it refers to present/future.
'It is time we left home.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He is working in this company since 2015.
He was working in this company since 2015.
He has been working in this company since 2015.
He has worked in this company since 2015.
questions.explanation:
For an ongoing action from a past point to the present, use Present Perfect Continuous with 'since'.
'He has been working in this company since 2015.' ✓
Simple Present Continuous (A) with 'since' is incorrect. Past Continuous (B) implies the action ended.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'If I ___ the answer, I would have told you.'
questions.explanation:
Third Conditional (unreal past): If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
'If I had known the answer, I would have told you.' ✓
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the correct verb form:
'I ___ my work when you called.'
questions.explanation:
Past Perfect is used for an action completed just before another past action.
'I had just finished my work when you called.' ✓
questions.subject: English
